Tom Brady. Peyton Manning. those two names define the NFL for the past decade and a half or so. Manning holds or is close to every notable passing record in football, and Brady doesn't just got "dem" rings,he's also appeared in more Super Bowls than any other QB ever and defines "winning" even more than Charlie Sheen. Both are first ballot Canton bound. Needless to say we pigskin fanatics all pay attention and throw in our two cents of our preference when the two square off, even if football is more of a team game than any other major commercialized sport. So as Brady-Manning 17 looms with a trip to the Super Bowl on the line let's take a closer look at their head to head match-ups:

The mouth breathers will say Brady is 11-5 vs Manning, settled score. But they're discounting a lot. In the case of this a playoff game, first and foremost, the series in the playoffs, when both their respective teams are at their best, the series is tied 2-2. But Brady still holds a decisive advantage overall right? Not so fast. When we adjust for other factors it's pretty close.

Brady leads the head to head series 11-5. However, once you start looking at home field advantage and streaky teams the numbers change:

Brady won the first six match-ups between the two, but even the biggest Brady booster can't argue that in his first few years as a starter Brady was most important piece of that early portion of the Patriots dynasty, with him statistically playing in the center of the pack of NFL QBs, while Peyton was the key piece to preventing an Indy team from jumping town to LA from day one. Four of those games were in Boston, with two in Indy. Then Peyton, with the height of the Colts and a Tony Dungy around him rolled off three wins in a row, including two in Boston. In the next three years Brady got a 2-1 advantage in games that were all one score wins, including getting a win in Peyton's house. Then Peyton missed a year for neck surgery and when he came back Tom has had a 3-1 advantage...never mind that Tom has won all the games in Boston and Peyton the lone game in Denver with Broncos fans complaining Tom and the Patriots being the beneficiary of multiple home games vs the Broncos because of schedule anomalies (possibly a legit complaint).

But at the end of the day Tom has won three times in Peytons house, while Peyton has won twice in Tom's house in 16 games. What does that mean? The team that is the home team wins a lot, and when you factor in the 2-2 playoff record both hold against each other it screams it. We fans like to think of QB vs QB, but it is team vs team, and all other things equal the home team has an advantage.

Let's dive to the stats. Head to head Brady has 4,013 passing yards, 32 touchdowns and 14 interceptions in games vs Manning. Manning has 4,809 passing yards, 33 touchdowns and 22 interceptions in games vs Brady. Reasonably comparable. Peyton with more productivity but more turnovers, Tom with less yards but fewer turnovers. Peyton being the be all end all of his team's possessions more than Tom career wise it makes sense. In the end, "In the same ball park" though. The average margin of win between the two? Only roughly four and a half points.

So what do all these numbers mean? It means if history repeats most football fans are probably in for a heck of a show next Sunday as we see generational best v best for the 17th time, while Broncos and Patriots fans are gonna be on the edge of their seats.

Tom Brady. Peyton Manning. Hold onto your butts.

They already have successfully managed to land on solid on their last flight. There are a lot of reasons they want to move beyond that. I'll give three in no particular order:

  • Economic benefits: Landing a rocket entails turning around a thing that's about 13 stories tall going thousands of miles an hour an having it survive descent from atmosphere and land on a pad about the size of a football field. That requires a substantial amount of fuel. The problem is not the cost of the fuel, but the space and weight of the fuel. Instead of having lots of stuff that goes boom there, you could instead have additional cargo. This savings in fuel is accommodated by having a landing platform that's more optimally placed for landing.

  • Flexibility and Safety: A mobile platform also provides self evident benefits in terms of flight planning flexibility. In the future we may even be able to launch from these platforms with clear benefits. Also you generally want to spend as little time as possible above populated areas with rockets. Fixed landing sites constrain your options here quite a bit.

  • Advancing the Technology: The best way to advance anything is to push it to its limits and then try to get even more. SpaceX's longterm goals are far larger than most people realize. They don't want to send a man to Mars. They want to colonize it. Musk is aiming to have, in his lifetime, a million humans living on Mars. Thanks to complacency from the major corporations in rocketry in the US, the technology we're using today isn't substantially changed from cold war era technology. Landing a rocket back here is a huge step relative to where we were, but it's a baby step in term of Elon's goals. He wants to Mars colonial transporters regularly flowing between Earth and Mars. Being able to land your reusable rocket wherever in the world (... or other worlds) you want to is really just a pretty common sense goal. And if you can land them in our ultra thick atmosphere on a moving barge in the middle of the ocean while 14 foot waves are splashing it around, then you're pretty far along with that goal of being able to land just about anywhere.
